title: Sam Altman says people don’t really want an AI to act as CEO: ‘I think the world wants to know about the person’
excerpt: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he shifted his views about AI-related layoffs in part because he has seen how much humans value themselves over AI.
content_html:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says he doesn't believe people would want an AI to replace his job.

"I think for my job, for example, I think the world wants to know about the person that's going to be responsible for the decisions of a company, and who they're going to hold accountable if they make bad ones, and they don't really want an AI CEO," Altman said during an episode of "Invest Like The Best" published on Tuesday.

Altman's thinking on the matter may have evolved since last November, when he told the "Conversations with Tyler" podcast that it would be akin to a failure if another company beat OpenAI to replacing its CEO with an AI model.

"Shame on me if OpenAI is not the first big company run by an AI CEO," Altman said at the time.

The OpenAI CEO said that the focus on humanity is one of the reasons that AI hasn't "upended" the economy to the extent he originally expected.

"People have a great degree of trust and enjoyment in working with other people," he said on "Invest Like The Best." "And you can go hire an AI consultant right now, or talk to an AI sales rep right now, or hire an AI engineer or whatever — somehow most people seem to still really prefer interacting with a human."

Altman said he feels the same way, too.

"I definitely would much rather engage with a person than engage with an AI for almost everything," he said.

As an example, Altman said that even though AI models can create spectacular images, people still value human-made artwork.

"There's the joke about at this point, the signature on a piece of art is most of the value, but the truth of it is you want to know about the person behind it," he said. "You read a novel, you want to know about the person behind it."

Altman said this focus on preserving and valuing humanity is one of the reasons that he has shifted his views on whether the technology will lead to mass job displacement like the kind he previously theorized. He recently said that he was "delighted to be wrong" about the short-term impact on entry-level jobs after previously stating that AI would wipe out "entire classes" of jobs.

The debate between AI-created and human-created content is roiling everything from Instagram to the books on the shelves at Barnes & Noble.

Like Altman, others in the industry have said that they are putting an emphasis on human taste or judgment. Altman suggested that "taste" might not be the best word to capture what humans do better than AI, even as he expects the models to continue narrowing the number of things where AI lags behind human abilities.

"The world may need a new kind of word for the kind of judgment that people are very good at, that AIs seem to really deeply struggle with," he said.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 表示，他不相信人们会希望人工智能取代他的工作。

奥特曼在周二出版的《像最好的人一样投资》一集中说：“例如，我认为，就我的工作而言，我认为全世界都想知道谁将负责公司的决策，以及如果他们做出了错误的决定，他们将追究谁的责任，而他们并不真正想要一位人工智能首席执行官。”

自去年 11 月以来，Altman 对此事的想法可能已经发生了变化，当时他在“Conversations with Tyler”播客中表示，如果另一家公司击败 OpenAI，用 AI 模型取代其首席执行官，那将类似于失败。

“如果 OpenAI 不是第一家由 AI 首席执行官运营的大公司，我会感到羞耻，”Altman 当时说道。

这位OpenAI首席执行官表示，对人性的关注是人工智能没有像他最初预期的那样“颠覆”经济的原因之一。

“人们在与他人合作时有很大程度的信任和享受，”他在“像最好的那样投资”节目中说道。 “你现在可以聘请一名人工智能顾问，或者立即与人工智能销售代表交谈，或者聘请一名人工智能工程师或其他什么——不知何故，大多数人似乎仍然更喜欢与人类互动。”

奥特曼说他也有同样的感觉。

“我肯定更愿意与人打交道，而不是在几乎所有事情上与人工智能打交道，”他说。

奥特曼举例说，尽管人工智能模型可以创造出壮观的图像，但人们仍然重视人造艺术品。

“现在有一个笑话，一件艺术品上的签名是最有价值的，但事实是你想了解它背后的人，”他说。 “你读一本小说，你想了解小说背后的人。”

奥特曼表示，对保护和重视人性的关注是他改变观点的原因之一，即该技术是否会像他之前理论的那样导致大规模工作岗位流失。 他最近表示，他之前曾表示人工智能将消灭“所有类别”的工作岗位，但他对初级工作岗位的短期影响的看法“很高兴自己是错误的”。

人工智能创造的内容和人类创造的内容之间的争论正在搅乱一切，从 Instagram 到 Barnes & Noble 书架上的书籍。

与奥特曼一样，业内其他人也表示，他们正在强调人类的品味或判断力。 奥特曼表示，“品味”可能不是描述人类比人工智能做得更好的最佳词，尽管他预计这些模型将继续缩小人工智能落后于人类能力的事情的数量。

他说：“世界可能需要一种新的词来形容人们非常擅长的判断，而人工智能似乎确实在与之深深挣扎。”
